title: queue-advance output data
description: The DECISION — placements, holds, and the disclosure that carries them.

computed_at.description: The single instant the decision was computed against (ISO-8601 UTC).
computed_at.title: Computed At

decision.description: The call's top-level outcome: 'place' when at least one placement was decided, 'hold' when items are queued but none could be placed, 'empty' when nothing was queued at all. Three states, not two, because 'nothing to do' and 'something to do that I refused to guess at' are opposite situations for the human.
decision.title: Decision

placements.description: The decided placements, at most ``max_placements``, in the order they should be dispatched. A DECISION, not an action: this verb writes nothing (R3) — the actor consumes it.
placements.title: Placements

held.description: Every item that stays queued, each with its disclosed reason (R4). Never elided.
held.title: Held

held_counts.description: reason_code -> count over ``held``. The pre-aggregated numbers a morning brief renders ('3 items waiting on gpu capacity') so no consumer has to re-derive them and risk a different total.
held_counts.title: Held Counts

queued_total.description: How many items were in state 'queued' and in scope when the decision was computed.
queued_total.title: Queued Total

considered_clusters.description: The candidate cluster keys this call evaluated, after any ``clusters`` restriction. Disclosed because an empty or unexpectedly narrow candidate set is the likeliest cause of a surprising hold.
considered_clusters.title: Considered Clusters

occupancy.description: campaign_id -> occupied pool slots at decision time, from the ONE shared predicate ``state/queue_occupancy.occupied_slots`` (R9). The least-loaded input, published so the decision's arithmetic is checkable and so campaign-advance and queue-advance cannot come to different totals.
occupancy.title: Occupancy

brief.description: The deterministic one-paragraph disclosure the session relays VERBATIM into the y — code-computed from the fields above, never authored. §3: the human's y covers the placement, so the placement has to be in front of them in the same breath as the question.
brief.title: Brief

QueueClusterVerdict.description:
Why ONE cluster was or was not eligible for ONE item.

The per-cluster evidence behind a hold. R4 says an item never disappears
without a reason; a reason that says only "nothing matched" is a reason the
human cannot act on, so the decision carries its work.

eligible.description: True when this cluster satisfied every hard constraint.
eligible.title: Eligible

reason.description: The specific verdict — which constraint failed and against which configured value (e.g. 'walltime_sec 172800 > constraints.max_walltime 3:00:00'). Names WHICH walltime ceiling it compared, because clusters.yaml carries two that disagree by 8-16x (S11).
reason.title: Reason

occupied.description: Pool slots this cluster's campaign id already occupies, from the ONE shared predicate ``state/queue_occupancy.occupied_slots`` (R9). The least-loaded tie-break input, and a disclosed number rather than an inferred one — it counts OUR committed work, not the scheduler's queue.
occupied.title: Occupied

QueueClusterVerdict.title: queue-advance cluster verdict

QueueHoldback.description:
One item that stays QUEUED, with the reason stated (R4).

Never dropped, never guessed at. A held item is a normal outcome — under
§7 R3 the queue's 'queued' state is almost entirely PRE-GATE (awaiting a y,
consent, or placement), not awaiting capacity.

reason_code.description: The closed-vocabulary cause, so briefs can COUNT by cause ('3 items waiting on gpu capacity').
reason_code.title: Reason Code

reason.description: The human-readable statement of the same cause, specific enough to act on.
reason.title: Reason

considered.description: Every cluster evaluated and why each was rejected — empty only when no cluster could be evaluated at all.
considered.title: Considered

detail.description: Structured particulars behind ``reason`` (the unknown pin and its near-miss suggestions, the cap and its current value, the asks that found no host). Machine-readable so a later tier can act on the hold without re-parsing prose.
detail.title: Detail

QueueHoldback.title: queue-advance holdback

QueuePlacement.description:
One decided placement: this item, that cluster, and the disclosed why.

This is what §3 means by placement living INSIDE the y. The greenlight
binds to a spec and the spec names the cluster, so the brief must be able
to say "next: rv_sweep item 4 -> hoffman2 (carc at 2/2, item needs gpu)" —
every token of which comes from this object.

item_id.description: The intake item this decision is about.
item_id.title: Item Id

run_id.description: The item's COMPUTED run id when known (§10.S2) — the key a dispatcher claims on, and the key the occupancy predicate collapses onto.
run_id.title: Run Id

cluster.description: The chosen clusters.yaml top-level key. Never guessed: absent a qualifying cluster the item is HELD instead.
cluster.title: Cluster

campaign_id.description: The concrete ``<base>_<clusterkey>`` campaign id this placement implies, composed from the item's campaign_base and the chosen cluster key (campaign-multi-cluster.md §2). Null for an open-loop item. Composed, never parsed — a base routinely contains underscores, so splitting one back apart is a hazard.
campaign_id.title: Campaign Id

scheduler.description: The chosen cluster's scheduler family, disclosed because it changes what the run can promise (S11: SGE cannot enforce the canary success-gate). Validated against the live backend registry.
scheduler.title: Scheduler

ssh_target.description: The chosen cluster's ``user@host`` as resolved from config AT DECISION TIME, for disclosure only. A run's recorded ssh_target is stale-by-design and re-resolved at use; nothing downstream should consume this field as the live target.
ssh_target.title: Ssh Target

pinned.description: True when an explicit cluster pin decided this, not policy (R5). The brief must not present an operator's own choice back to them as the tool's recommendation.
pinned.title: Pinned

reason.description: The disclosed WHY, in one line, naming the deciding factor and the runner-up. This string is what the y is taken against, so it must state the actual rule that fired (pin / hard constraint elimination / least-loaded / alphabetical tie-break), never a summary of it.
reason.title: Reason

considered.description: Every cluster evaluated for this item, with its verdict — the evidence behind ``reason``, so a human can check the choice rather than trust it.
considered.title: Considered

QueuePlacement.title: queue-advance placement
